sentences.text: Notohypsilophodon was a small, bipedal herbivore belonging to the ornithopod dinosaur group from the Late Cretaceous of Argentina.
Gregory S. Paul estimated this creature measured just 1.3 meters in length and weighed only 6 kilograms.
Rubén D. Martínez named and described the species in 1998, giving it a specific name that refers to the city of Comodoro Rivadavia.
Martínez considered the individual a juvenile because its neural arches were not fused to the vertebrae bodies.
A recent redescription found Notohypsilophodon to be basal in Ornithopoda and more primitive than Gasparinisaura.
However, some researchers argue the fossil remains are too fragmentary to classify beyond Euornithopoda, a clade including hypsilophodonts and iguanodonts.
Notohypsilophodon lived from 100.5 to 89.8 million years ago during the Cenomanian to Turonian stages.
It is debated whether Notohypsilophodon was the only hypsilophodont known from South America, as Gasparinisaura is now considered a basal euornithopod as well.
